The nbfx Nodes API is the toolkit-free model of the property sheet: the PropertyModel of one property, the PropertySetModel that groups properties, and the PropertiesProvider that contributes sets for a context object.
Property providers return toolkit-free models. The platform property sheet renders them in JavaFX and adapts their change notifications to an observable value. A JavaFX-facing model, ObservablePropertyModel, lives in api.property so that providers which already use JavaFX properties can expose one without putting a toolkit type in this module. Explorer node/children models are added with their first view consumer in M1.
A provider contributes the properties of a file, an editor document or a project.
The property sheet shows those properties, in groups, with an expert toggle.
The user edits a writable property; the model notifies its listeners.
The model and its simple implementation are unit-tested. The API is under development.
A JDK is required only to compile.
Only org.netbeans.api.nbfx.nodes is public.
The platform property sheet finds PropertiesProvider implementations in the global Lookup.
Providers register themselves with @ServiceProvider(service = PropertiesProvider.class).

The model carries no thread affinity. The property sheet reads and updates it on the JavaFX thread; providers should be cheap.
